To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel decoys generation technique that can be used with any convolutional network and (2) we propose a new saliency score that is provably robust against gradient saturation and inter-feature dependence.

we propose a data driven technique that uses the decoys to infer a robust saliency map, which is applicable to any convolution network architecture and any existing off-the-shelf gradient based saliency methods and we empirically validate the proposed technique on ImageNet data set with three different network architectures and three saliency methods.

we proposed a data-driven technique to infer robust salient scores in conjunction with any pre-trained convolutional network classifier and any saliency method by using distribution-preserving decoy pixels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of robust saliency maps that can be used to interpret predictions of deep neural networks in a wide variety of applications.

our method is able to generate more robust saliency maps in the presence of adversarial attacks.
our method improves the robustness of saliency maps by compensating for gradient saturation and considering the joint activation patterns of the input pixels in a single layer of a CNN.
our proposed method is a simple and effective approach to generate decoys for robust saliency maps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed decoy-enhanced approach is a generic and data-driven method to improve the performance of existing saliency scores.
the proposed method can be used to enhance the saliency scores of any existing saliency method, which is a general and powerful technique to improve the robustness of saliency maps.
the proposed data-driven technique can be used to improve saliency methods by generating robust saliency maps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution-preserving property of decoys is crucial for robust saliency maps, which can be used for better understanding of deep neural network models.
distribution-preserving decoy generation is an important and effective technique for improving the robustness and interpretability of saliency maps.
decoys can be used to improve existing saliency scores.
